title: The LCD: Adding and Subtracting Fractions
subject: Mathematics

scenes.heading: The LCD
scenes.subheading: Grade 8 Mathematics · HCF, LCM and LCD, part 3
scenes.narration: Welcome to part three of our series on the H C F, the L C M and the L C D. In this lesson we use the lowest common denominator to add and subtract fractions.

scenes.heading: What is the LCD?
bullets: To add or subtract fractions, the denominators must be the same
The LCD is the LCM of the denominators
Multiply the top and the bottom by the same number
scenes.narration: To add or subtract fractions, the denominators, the bottom numbers, must be the same. The L C D is the lowest common denominator. It is simply the L C M of the denominators. To change a fraction to the L C D, multiply the top and the bottom by the same number, so its value does not change.

scenes.heading: Example 1
scenes.narration: Work out one quarter plus one sixth. The L C D is the L C M of four and six, which is twelve. One quarter is three twelfths: multiply the top and the bottom by three. One sixth is two twelfths: multiply the top and the bottom by two. Three twelfths plus two twelfths is five twelfths.

scenes.heading: Example 2: Subtracting
scenes.narration: Work out five sixths minus three eighths. The L C M of six and eight is twenty four, so the L C D is twenty four. Five sixths is twenty twenty-fourths, because we multiply the top and the bottom by four. Three eighths is nine twenty-fourths, because we multiply by three. Twenty minus nine is eleven, so the answer is eleven twenty-fourths.

scenes.heading: Example 3: Three fractions
scenes.narration: Work out two thirds plus three quarters minus five sixths. The L C M of three, four and six is twelve. Two thirds is eight twelfths. Three quarters is nine twelfths. Five sixths is ten twelfths. Eight plus nine minus ten is seven. The answer is seven twelfths.

scenes.heading: Example 4: Mixed numbers
scenes.narration: Work out one and a half plus two and two thirds. Add the whole numbers first: one plus two is three. Then the fractions, with an L C D of six: one half is three sixths, and two thirds is four sixths. Three sixths plus four sixths is seven sixths, which is one and one sixth. So the answer is four and one sixth.

scenes.heading: Example 5: With a variable
scenes.narration: The same method works in algebra. Simplify x over two plus x over three. The L C D is six. x over two is three x over six. x over three is two x over six. Three x plus two x is five x, so the answer is five x over six.

scenes.heading: Tips
bullets: Find the LCD first: the LCM of the denominators
Whatever you do to the bottom, do to the top
Add or subtract the tops only, never the bottoms
scenes.narration: Four tips. Find the L C D first: it is the L C M of the denominators. Whatever you multiply the bottom by, multiply the top by the same number. Add or subtract the top numbers only, never the bottom numbers. And simplify your answer at the end. For example, three sixths simplifies to one half.

activity.title: Adding and subtracting fractions with the LCD
activity.instructions: Work out. Give your answer in its simplest form.
